videos.title: Fetch, check and label, then rehearse: loading, linking and initialization, and why reading a constant never wakes its class
A stand-in at the stage door: Proxy writes an ordinary final class, and every call becomes one invoke with a Method and an Object array
Most boxes are thrown out young: eden, survivor copies, ages on the label, promotion to the old generation, and a cost that follows what survives
G1 cuts the heap into equal regions and collects the most garbage first
From the interpreter to C1 to C2: why the same code gets faster the longer it runs
A nanoTime loop measures the optimizer: dead code, constant folding, and the loop JMH builds instead
False sharing: two threads, two fields, one cache line bouncing between cores
Leyden's AOT cache: train, assemble, then start with the classes already loaded and linked
From a heap dump to the leak: retained size and the dominator tree
The cue that says ask the director: invokedynamic calls its bootstrap method once, then calls the linked target directly
Reading a flame graph: width is samples, left to right is the alphabet, and the wide tops are where to start
The label on every box: a 12-byte header, the fields in the JVM's order, padding to 8, and 4-byte references below 32 GB
A tour of the container: wiring by reflection, interceptors through proxies, then the same wiring generated at build time
Native image builds a closed world: only code reachable from main gets in, so a class named at run time needs a metadata entry
A started JVM is still cold: CRaC saves a warm process to disk and restores it, once your resources let go
A stagehand with hooks and a pile of cue cards: the operand stack runs seconds(32, 12500) in seven instructions, and a long takes two slots
A stretch of shelf for every worker: new bumps a pointer in the thread's own TLAB, and C2 skips a box that never leaves the desk
ZGC moves objects while threads run: colored references and a load barrier that fixes stale ones on the next load
The crew keeps what the notes from the roots can reach: strong, soft, weak and phantom holds, and why soft and weak caches forget
A Java agent's transformer sees each class's bytes as the JVM defines it; retransformation swaps method bodies under live objects, never the class's shape
Inlining: C2 copies a small method into its caller, within a budget of 35 bytes, or 325 at a hot call
The crew's logbook: reading one GC log line field by field, and telling pauses from work that runs beside your threads
The kitchen's log book: JFR records what the JVM did, on one clock, cheap enough to leave on
Byte Buddy sews a subclass while the program runs: each override calls an interceptor, and whatever is final stays out of reach
Every launch runs the same morning routine: create the VM, then unpack and check each class the first time it is needed (818 for a one-class demo)
The kitchen that stops to wash up: start from the slow tail and the GC count, find the line that allocates, fix one thing at a time
A class file is a page with a strict layout: the CAFEBABE stamp, the version, then a constant pool where each tag sets the entry's size and a Long takes two numbers

An interceptor runs around a call and proceed() hands it on: a JDK proxy for a component with interfaces, a Byte Buddy subclass for one without, and retry only the smallest call that is safe to repeat

A reflective start finds components, reads annotations, orders the graph and has Byte Buddy write a subclass: 2,207 classes and 1,029 ms; the same wiring generated at build time leaves only holders: 991 classes and 266 ms
